title: Month-end close
blurb: Accruals, intercompany, subledger close and the exception pack, filed before the controller opens her laptop.
description: How Anvil closes the books for six entities in four hours, and what it hands to the controller.
content:
Close is not one task. It is four hundred small ones, most of which are the same every month, performed by people who are too senior to be doing them at eleven at night.

What the agent does

Anvil starts two days before close. It reads open items across every entity, matches them against the close checklist your team already maintains, and posts what is unambiguous — accruals with a prior-period pattern, intercompany balances that net to zero, recurring journals with an unchanged basis.

  • 41 journal entries posted per entity on an average month
  • 3 to 9 exceptions raised with the reasoning attached
  • Every posting reversible from the ledger, by batch

What it does not do

It does not decide materiality. It does not sign anything. Anything outside the checklist becomes an exception with a named owner and the evidence it used, and it waits.

The first month it ran, it found a recurring accrual we had been posting twice since a 2024 reorganisation.

Getting there

Two weeks. One week connecting to a sandbox copy of your tenant and reading a completed close, one week running in parallel against the live one while your team watches the ledger and disagrees with it.

title: Three-way invoice matching
blurb: Invoice against purchase order against receipt, with contract terms checked and duplicates held before the payment run.
description: Matching every invoice to its order and receipt, and holding the duplicates before they are paid.
content:
Duplicate payments are not an accounts payable failure. They are a volume problem: nobody can read forty thousand invoices a quarter carefully, so a percentage of them go out twice.

What the agent does

Every inbound invoice is matched against its purchase order and its goods receipt, then against the contract that governs the order — payment terms, agreed rates, volume breaks. Mismatches are held rather than routed, with the specific line and the specific clause quoted.

  • Duplicates caught on supplier, amount, date proximity and reference distance
  • Rate variances checked against the contract, not the last invoice
  • Held items appear in the buyer's queue with a one-line reason

The number

Across the first four customers, £1.2m of duplicate and over-rate invoices were held before payment in the first two quarters. None of it was fraud. All of it was volume.

title: Access reviews
runtime: Runs quarterly, and on every leaver
blurb: The quarterly attestation pack assembled from the real entitlement data, with dormant accounts revoked on the same run.
description: Quarterly access reviews assembled from live entitlement data instead of a stale spreadsheet.
content:
Access review season is a spreadsheet exercise: export the entitlements, chase the managers, paste the answers back, hope the export was current.

What the agent does

Anvil reads live entitlements from the identity provider and the applications themselves, groups them by manager, and asks each one only about what changed since the last review. Dormant accounts — no authentication in ninety days, no ticket, no exception — are proposed for revocation with the evidence attached.

  • 2,400 accounts reviewed per quarter without a spreadsheet leaving the building
  • Revocations executed on approval, reversible for thirty days
  • The attestation pack assembled as the review runs, not after it

What auditors get

A record of who was asked, what they saw, what they said, and what changed as a result — with timestamps that come from the systems rather than from an email thread.

title: Joiner and leaver runs
blurb: Policy answers, benefits changes and the twenty-three tasks that follow a start date, filed against the right records.
description: Onboarding, offboarding and the policy questions that surround them, handled inside the HCM.
content:
People operations is interrupt-driven work. A start date moves and twenty-three downstream tasks move with it; a policy question arrives that has been answered four hundred times.

What the agent does

Anvil answers from your policy documents, with the clause quoted and linked, and files the tasks a status change implies: equipment, access, payroll cutoffs, probation dates, benefits windows. Anything that touches pay or contract terms goes to a person.

  • 71% of inbound questions answered without a person touching them
  • 23 downstream tasks refiled automatically when a start date moves
  • Every answer carries the policy version it was based on

title: Variance packs
runtime: Runs on the first working day
blurb: Actuals against budget across every entity, with the flux commentary drafted from the underlying transactions.
description: Variance packs and flux commentary built from the transactions rather than the summary.
content:
The variance is easy. The commentary is the work — and it is written from a summary, by someone who then goes back to the transactions to find out what actually happened.

What the agent does

Anvil starts at the transactions. It reads the movements behind each variance over threshold, groups them by cause, and drafts commentary that names the cause rather than restating the number. The pack is assembled per entity and consolidated.

  • Six entities packed and consolidated before the first working day begins
  • Commentary cites the transactions it was drawn from
  • Thresholds are yours, and they are visible in the pack

What the FP&A team does instead

Edits. The draft is wrong often enough to be interesting and right often enough to be worth reading first.
